diary-of-a-ceo-january-2026.title: Diary of a CEO — January 2026 Kiriakou interview
diary-of-a-ceo-january-2026.summary: The January 2026 long-form appearance by John Kiriakou on Steven Bartlett's Diary of a CEO podcast that a University of Texas at Austin sophomore then cut into TikTok shorts — sped and slowed, with lasers added — kicking off the Gen Z discovery of Kiriakou that pushed his cameo requests past 1,900 and drew a 2:30 a.m. representation call in Dubai from the Creative Artists Agency; Kiriakou treats it as the pivot after which stories he had been telling for nineteen years finally landed.

data.Downstream effect: TikTok shorts by a UT Austin sophomore triggered the Gen Z breakout

dyk: … that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) had *"been telling the same stories for nineteen years"* before a single January 2026 [Diary of a CEO](/wiki/diary-of-a-ceo-january-2026) appearance — cut into TikTok shorts by a University of Texas at Austin sophomore with sped voice, slowed voice and laser eyes — made him Gen Z's most-shared former CIA officer overnight?

… that after a niece told [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) *"you're exploding on TikTok,"* the [Creative Artists Agency](/wiki/diary-of-a-ceo-january-2026) called him at 2:30 in the morning in Dubai to sign him — *"Tell me you're not represented"* — and closed the deal on the spot?
diary-of-a-ceo-january-2026.body:
The **Diary of a CEO — January 2026 Kiriakou interview** is the long-form podcast appearance by [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) on Steven Bartlett's *Diary of a CEO* that, in Kiriakou's own account, produced the pivot he calls his Gen Z breakout.<Cite t="19:10" /> Kiriakou describes the interview itself as *"the standard long-form podcast interview"* he had already given many times to [Tucker Carlson](/wiki/tucker-carlson) and Joe Rogan, only *"a little bit more philosophical."* He recorded it, boarded a plane and flew home; the shorts came later.<Cite t="19:41" />

## The UT Austin sophomore's shorts

A University of Texas at Austin sophomore took the Bartlett interview and cut it into TikTok shorts — *"sped up my voice, slowed down my voice, shot lasers out of my eyes"* — and, in Kiriakou's telling, *"it went completely crazy."*<Cite t="20:13" /> While Kiriakou was on a paid contract in Dubai, his niece called: *"Uncle John, you're exploding on TikTok — I don't know why, but it's huge."* At 2:30 the following morning local time, the [Creative Artists Agency](/wiki/diary-of-a-ceo-january-2026) — *"the biggest talent agency in the world"* — reached him and said *"tell me you're not represented."* He wasn't. They signed him on the call.<Cite t="20:44" />

## Why he thinks it landed with Gen Z

Kiriakou attributes the traction to a generational appetite for a truth-teller with no personal agenda: *"Gen Z trusts me because I'm a truth-teller — I don't have any personal agenda, none. I think that for the most part, mainstream media lies to us every single day."* His prescription to the audience is not a subscription but a discipline: sample twenty-five outlets across the ideological range — the *Washington Post*, *New York Times*, *Wall Street Journal*, *LA Times*, BBC, *Times of London*, AP, Reuters, Al Jazeera, Al Monitor — and reason your way to the fact pattern yourself.<Cite t="21:15" /><Cite t="21:45" /><Cite t="22:18" />

kiriakou-cameo-practice.title: Kiriakou cameo practice
kiriakou-cameo-practice.summary: John Kiriakou's post-2026 use of the Cameo personalised-video service — running at roughly 25 to 30 hours a week, some 900 messages in the month of March 2026 alone, nearly 2,000 messages in total by July 2026 — that he says has produced three cases in which the person receiving the video message afterwards told him he had talked them out of committing suicide, including a 15-year-old bulimic girl to whom Kiriakou gave his personal phone number.

data.Volume: ≈25–30 hours/week; 900 messages in March 2026; ≈1,950 total by July 2026
data.Pep talks: ≈10 percent of requests; three afterwards credited him with talking them out of suicide

dyk: … that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) has recorded roughly 1,950 personalised video messages on Cameo — 900 of them in March 2026 alone — running at 25 to 30 hours a week, and that three of the recipients afterwards told him his message had talked them out of committing suicide, part of his [cameo practice](/wiki/kiriakou-cameo-practice)?

… that in one [Cameo pep talk](/wiki/kiriakou-cameo-practice), [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) broke the platform's rules to give his personal phone number to a 15-year-old bulimic girl who had said she was going to kill herself — and that she called him crying that same day, then twice more since, *"very respectful,"* just to hear a friendly voice on a down day?
kiriakou-cameo-practice.body:
The **Kiriakou cameo practice** is [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou)'s use of the Cameo personalised-video service to send messages to paying strangers, at a volume he describes as *"probably 25 or 30 hours a week"* — 900 messages in March 2026 alone and, on his own July 2026 count, *"about 1,950 cameos so far."*<Cite t="1:07:18" /><Cite t="1:07:50" /><Cite t="1:08:22" />

He estimates that about half of the requests are birthday wishes, roughly ten percent are pep talks, and that of the pep talks *"three have come back to say that I somehow talked them out of committing suicide. I'm not really sure how I did that. But, you know, there are a lot of really hurting people out there."*<Cite t="1:08:22" /><Cite t="1:08:52" />

## The fifteen-year-old bulimic girl

One pep-talk recipient sounded, in Kiriakou's account, in such acute pain that he violated Cameo's rules on the recorded message itself: *"We're not supposed to do this, but here's my phone number — call me."* She called him within the hour, crying: fifteen years old, bulimic, parents who did not understand her, planning to kill herself. He talked her out of it. She has called him twice since, *"usually for less than a minute or two — very respectful,"* just to hear a friendly voice on a down day.<Cite t="1:08:52" /><Cite t="1:09:23" /><Cite t="1:09:54" />
